svg.desc: Two columns of bars on one vertical axis in bits per bet, drawn in proportion to the numbers. The left column, definition one, compares growth with and without the signal at the same prices. Its first bar, with the report, is 0.277 high, made of a lower segment of 0.041 and an upper segment of 0.236; its second bar, without the report, is the lower segment alone, 0.041. A bracket beside the second bar marks the difference, Delta = 0.236. Below the column: given what the investor without the report uses, by default publicly available information, here the same as what the price-setters have seen; it equals the mutual information in a horse-race market and is at most the mutual information in a general stock market. The right column, definition two, a belief bet against the price, has one bar with the report, 0.277 high, split into the amount of information I(θ; Y), undiffused, 0.236, above, and the price's own error D(π ‖ q), undigested, 0.041, below. Below the column: given what the price-setters have seen; it equals the mutual information only if the price is calibrated, q = π. The 0.236 segments share one color and the 0.041 segments another, so the part subtracted on the left is the part kept on the right. A footer says that both columns use the same conditioning set: the investor without the report uses what the price-setters have seen, so she holds 0.30; prior 0.30, report right 80% of the time, price 0.20, bits per bet, our calculation.
